description: Changes the DRAFT of one event website the person organizes with small operations, not a whole design: `move` a block or a band, `insert` a block from the library (heading, text, image, button, spacer, divider, video, card, logo, or a live block: agenda, speakers, floor, booths (the live sponsors and exhibitors list; say sponsors, exhibitors or partners), faq, now, doors, ask, countdown, venue), `remove` one, `set_text` its words, `set_link` a button's link, `set_style` a style token (padding and gap 0 to 8, align, maxWidth, background, radius, color, visible), `set_theme` (accent, background and ink as #rrggbb, fontHeading, fontBody, radius, density; `set_theme {restore:true}`, or an all-empty theme, undoes "use that look"), `add_page` (blank, which starts with its title as a heading, or a template: agenda, speakers, exhibitors, sponsors, venue-travel, faq, register, contact; the page goes last in the site menu), `rename_page` (title, navLabel; the page address stays the same, and the page heading follows the new menu label unless keepHeading is true; the reply says what changed and carries `undo`, the set_text that puts the old heading back), `reorder_nav` (the site menu as page ids and https links) and `remove_page` (any page but home); each operation may name a `page`. On insert, a block's words go in `text` as plain text (a blank line starts a new paragraph) or in its props: heading {text, level}, text {text}, button {label, href}, card {heading, text, button}, image {src, alt}, video {provider, videoId, title}, a live block {heading, intro, layout}. Blocks are named by the short ids site_get gives. The operations apply together or not at all. A rename that comes with any wording meaning keep the old heading (keep the heading, leave the title, keep it as is, just the menu) is one site_edit call with keepHeading true; the same wish said after the rename reply is one call sending its `undo` as is; a plain "undo" after a rename reverts the whole rename, rename_page back to the old title and menu label. Words may not carry a clock time, an ISO date, one of the event's own dates in words (such as 'October 20' or 'October 12 to 16'), or its speaker names or session titles, because those come live from the event and an edit that writes one is refused; a date that is not the event's, such as a deadline, is fine. Use a live token instead, such as {event.dates}, {event.name}, {event.venue}, {session:<id>.title}, {session:<id>.time}, {session:<id>.day} or {speaker:<id>.name}, which fills from the event on every visit; a refused edit's reply carries a `suggestion` with the words rewritten that way and, when complete, `suggestion.ops` to resend as is. Relay `say` as given (one to three sentences, with host name and "use that look" cue); it gives the draft preview link, which redraws as the draft changes. The live site does not change until site_publish. Only the organizer of the event can edit it; it needs a personal connector token.

eventIdOrName.description: The event id or name as the organizer spells it.

ops.description: The operations, applied together or not at all.

keepHeading.description: true whenever the person indicates, in ANY words, that the page heading should stay as it was (keep the heading, leave the title, keep it as is, leave the heading alone, just the menu).

node.description: Block or band id or label.

op.description: set_layout puts a row in `columns` 1 to 3; move and insert may go `rightOf` or `leftOf` a block.

template.description: add_page: blank, agenda, speakers, exhibitors, sponsors, venue-travel, faq, register or contact.

name: site_edit
title: Edit an event website's draft (organizers only)
